summary: Reviewed 2 test files: pipeline-duration.test.ts (3 new tests) and work-package-schema.test.ts (2 new tests).
All 3 pipeline-duration tests follow correct patterns: mkdtemp for isolation, process.argv save/restore, meaningful ±1s timing window for the computation test.
Invalid started_at test correctly uses 'as any' to bypass TypeScript type constraints to exercise the runtime guard. Well-commented.
Both Zod schema tests use proper safeParse + if(result.success) guard before accessing result.data. Backward-compatibility test correctly verifies duration_ms is undefined when omitted.
No security concerns. Cleanup uses rm with { recursive: true, force: true } on known temp paths.

comments.note: All 3 tests use a unique mkdtemp-generated tempLedgerRoot per test run, so parallel vitest workers cannot conflict even though PLAN_PATH is a static constant. The static slug is safe because LedgerStore uses tempLedgerRoot (unique) for actual I/O. Process.argv save/restore is correctly scoped to beforeEach/afterEach.

The 'as any' cast in test 3 for invalid started_at is the correct approach — it bypasses the TypeScript ISO string constraint to test the runtime guard in completePipeline. The comment explaining why is present. Pattern is consistent with test isolation principles.
No observations — test code is clean, minimal, and well-focused. Each test verifies exactly one behavior.
